title: Internal displacement is becoming a structural crisis as conflict, disasters, repeated movements, and weak data systems compound
source_unit: Internal Displacement Monitoring Centre, 2026 Global Report on Internal Displacement
geography: Global, with regional overviews covering 104 countries and territories

observations.period: 2025; people living in internal displacement at year end

denominator.unit: countries and territories covered by the global estimate

idp_stock.unit: million internally displaced people at end-2025

long_run_change.value: more than doubled over the decade, from 38.9 million in 2016 to 82.2 million in 2025

drivers.value: conflict, violence, and disasters, many intensified by climate change, drove internal displacement

structural_frame.value: internal displacement is described as a global structural crisis rather than a short-lived emergency alone

observations.method: IDMC global aggregation of country-level estimates and internal-displacement event data, supported by regional overviews, maps, charts, and publication synthesis.
observations.uncertainty: Coverage, definitions, reporting quality, and estimation methods vary across countries; the global stock is a year-end estimate and does not identify every person who moved or returned during the year.
observations.subgroup: Internally displaced people, people exposed to conflict or disasters, host communities, national and local authorities, humanitarian organizations, and service providers.
observations.counterinterpretation: A large stock can reflect improved detection and reporting as well as worsening displacement; people counted in the stock may have very different durations, needs, coping resources, and prospects for return or integration.

conflict_change.value: conflict-related internal displacements increased 60 percent compared with 2024

repeat_movement.value: protracted and intensifying conflicts can force people to move repeatedly, adding to annual displacement while enlarging the year-end stock

political_consequence.value: internal displacement links security shocks to housing, services, livelihoods, local authority capacity, and durable-solution politics within countries

response_route.value: durable solutions require more than physical movement away from immediate danger, including recovery, safety, services, livelihoods, and rights

observations.method: IDMC comparison of annual conflict-related internal displacements and year-end displacement stocks across its global monitoring coverage.
observations.uncertainty: Annual displacement events are movements rather than unique people; the same person can be displaced multiple times, and the report does not establish a causal forecast for future conflicts.
observations.subgroup: People displaced by conflict or violence, people repeatedly displaced, host communities, local authorities, peace and humanitarian actors, and livelihood providers.
observations.counterinterpretation: Higher event counts may partly reflect better event detection or reporting; a fall in annual movements would not necessarily mean that the accumulated displaced population has recovered or found a durable solution.

east_asia_pacific.unit: million conflict- and disaster-related internal displacements in East Asia and the Pacific in 2025

sub_saharan_africa.unit: million internal displacements in Sub-Saharan Africa in 2025

sub_saharan_stock.unit: million internally displaced people in Sub-Saharan Africa at end-2025

regional_asymmetry.value: regional exposure differs in both event flows and accumulated stocks, with conflict the primary driver in Sub-Saharan Africa and disaster and conflict both prominent in East Asia and the Pacific

observations.method: IDMC regional aggregation of internal-displacement events and year-end stocks, with regional narrative interpretation.
observations.uncertainty: Regional aggregates combine countries with different data systems and event profiles; event totals and stocks are not interchangeable and should not be read as a single affected-person count.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people and host communities across East Asia and the Pacific and Sub-Saharan Africa, including populations exposed to conflict, disasters, and climate-related hazards.
observations.counterinterpretation: High event totals can coexist with rapid returns or short-duration movements, while a lower event total can coexist with a large unresolved stock; regional averages conceal substantial country and subnational variation.

data_system_route.value: the report includes a chapter on resilient and sustainable displacement data systems

measurement_function.value: reliable, comparable, and sustained data are treated as infrastructure for targeting assistance, coordinating actors, and tracking progress toward solutions

local_state_capacity.value: local and national governments and partners are central to turning displacement evidence into protection, recovery, services, and durable solutions

feedback_loop.value: displacement data can shape resource allocation and public accountability, while weak data systems can make needs and recovery gaps less visible

observations.method: IDMC review of displacement measurement practice, country and regional evidence, and solution-oriented response requirements.
observations.uncertainty: Data-system recommendations do not by themselves demonstrate that measurement produces better outcomes; institutional incentives, privacy, access, interoperability, funding, and local trust affect implementation.
observations.subgroup: Displaced people, host communities, local and national governments, statistical and humanitarian data producers, funders, and organizations responsible for recovery and durable solutions.
observations.counterinterpretation: More data can impose reporting burdens or create privacy and protection risks if governance is weak; some forms of displacement and unmet need remain difficult to measure even in well-funded systems.

Official summary page for the report's global findings and response framing.

boundary: This record adds a global conflict, disaster, mobility, durable-solutions, and displacement-data route using IDMC aggregate estimates and publication analysis. It does not contain respondent-level displacement histories, individual location trajectories, household files, causal conflict forecasts, person-level service needs, or proof that every displaced population follows the same path.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official IDMC 2026 report page and global report page reviewed for the 82.2 million year-end stock, 104-country coverage, decade increase, conflict and disaster drivers, regional totals, repeated displacement framing, and displacement-data-system chapter.
